name: com.vibedgames/platform
title: vibedgames
description: A game studio for coding agents: skills, asset generation, and one-step deploys of browser games.

tools.name: credits
tools.description: Returns the caller's generation credit balance in micro-USD (1,000,000 = $1), their 100 most recent ledger entries, whether card purchases are open, and whether the caller must confirm their email before redeeming a code.

tools.name: credits_buy
tools.description: Starts a card payment for `amountUsd` of generation credit and returns a hosted checkout URL for a person to open. The credit lands once the payment clears, usually within seconds of paying. 412 while card purchases aren't open (`purchasesEnabled` is false on `credits.me`).

amountUsd.description: Whole dollars of credit to buy, 5–500. One dollar paid is one dollar of credit.

tools.name: credits_redeem
tools.description: Redeems a credit code for the caller, adding its value to their balance. Each account can redeem a given code once. 403 when the code is unknown, expired, revoked or used up; 409 when this account already redeemed it; 412 until the account's email address is confirmed.

code.description: The credit code to redeem, as you were given it, e.g. `ABC123`; case and surrounding spaces don't matter

tools.name: deploy
tools.description: Deploys a game. The usual way: pass `bundle: true`, PUT a gzipped tar of the built game (`tar -czf game.tgz -C dist .`, `index.html` at its root) to the `bundleUpload` URL it returns, then call again with the `deploymentId` and `publish: true`; publish unpacks it. Files can also be given one by one: `files` carries `utf-8` text, or with `encoding: url` the URL of an asset generate made, which the server fetches itself (up to 32 MB a call); `presign` takes a file's path, size and SHA-256 and returns a signed PUT URL for it in `uploads`. Upload URLs are on this server and last 15 minutes. A call without `deploymentId` stages a new deployment beside the live one; later calls pass it back to add or replace files. `publish: true` requires `index.html` and every presigned file at its declared size, makes the deployment live at `{slug}.vibedgames.com` and only then removes the previous one, so the game never goes dark mid-upload. With `source: true` publish also keeps the deployment's files as the game's forkable source (up to 64 MB); a caller with its own source archive passes `sourceArchive` instead and PUTs it to `sourceUpload`. 403 when the slug belongs to someone else.

bundle.description: true returns a `bundleUpload` URL to PUT the whole built game to as one gzipped tar, `index.html` at its root (`tar -czf game.tgz -C dist .`); a later call with `publish: true` unpacks it. The usual way in. Default false

deploymentId.description: The `deploymentId` an earlier deploy call for this slug returned, to add files to that staged deployment or publish it; omit to stage a new one

files.description: Files sent in the call itself: text, or a generated asset's URL with `encoding: url`. A path already staged is replaced. Default none

content.description: The file's text, or with `encoding: url` a generated asset's URL

contentType.description: The MIME type to serve the file with, e.g. `text/html; charset=utf-8`; omit to infer it from the path's extension

encoding.description: How to read `content`: `utf-8` (the default) stores it as the file's text; `url` fetches it from a URL a generate tool returned (other hosts are refused), up to 10 MB a file and 32 MB a call

path.description: The file's path from the game's root, e.g. `index.html` or `assets/hero.png`; no leading `/` and no `..`

name.description: The game's display name, up to 120 characters, e.g. `Space Pong`; omit to keep the name it has

presign.description: Files you PUT yourself: each returns a signed URL in `uploads`, valid 15 minutes, to PUT its bytes to with the `headers` given; list a file again to renew its URL. Default none

contentType.description: The MIME type to serve the file with, and the Content-Type to PUT it with, e.g. `image/png`; omit to infer it from the path's extension

path.description: The file's path from the game's root, e.g. `index.html` or `assets/hero.png`; no leading `/` and no `..`

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes as 64 hex characters, as `sha256sum` prints it

size.description: The file's exact size in bytes, at most 10485760 (10 MB); publish checks the uploaded file has this size

publish.description: true makes the staged deployment live at `{slug}.vibedgames.com` once this call's files are in (it needs `index.html` and every presigned file at its declared size), then removes the previous one. Default false: the files stay staged

slug.description: The game's slug, which makes its address `{slug}.vibedgames.com`: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no hyphen at either end, e.g. `space-pong`. A new slug becomes your game, one another account owns is refused; pass the same one on every call of a deployment

source.description: With `publish: true`, also keep the deployment's files (up to 64 MB) as the game's forkable source, which fork downloads. Default false; not with `sourceArchive`

sourceArchive.description: Your own forkable source archive (a .tar.gz of the project, what `vg deploy --source` packs), which you PUT to the `sourceUpload` URL this call returns; omit for none. Not with `source: true`

bytes.description: The archive's exact size in bytes, at most 104857600 (100 MB); publish checks the upload has this size

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the archive's bytes as 64 hex characters

tools.name: deployments
tools.description: Lists the caller's games, most recently updated first, each with its live deployment.

tools.name: deployments_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes one of the caller's games and all of its deployed files.

gameId.description: The id of one of your games: a game's `id` in the deployments list, or the `gameId` deploy returned

tools.name: fork
tools.description: Returns a one-hour download URL for a game's forkable source archive. Any signed-in user may fork any game that shipped source. Backs `vg fork`.

slug.description: The slug of the game to fork, as in its address `{slug}.vibedgames.com`, e.g. `space-pong`; any game deployed with source can be forked

tools.name: games_browse
tools.description: Browses the games on vibedgames, as the site's gallery shows them: each with its description, tags (`3d`, `camera` for webcam control, `multiplayer`), cover image and the URL it plays at. `query` matches words in a name, description or tag; `tag` keeps only games with it. Hosts with MCP Apps render it as a gallery to play from.

query.description: Words to match against a game's name, description and tags

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Runs a model to generate an image, video, audio clip, 3D model or text, billed against your credits. Pass the endpoint id and the model's input (see generate_schema). Waits up to `wait_seconds` for the result; a job still running by then returns its `request_id` and status, to follow with generate_status. Needs a positive credit balance (403 `insufficient_credits`) and a priced model (400 `unknown_endpoint`).

endpoint_id.description: A model's endpoint id, as generate models lists it, e.g. `fal-ai/flux/dev`

input.description: The model's input, per generate schema

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_docs
tools.description: Searches the model documentation: how a model is prompted, what its inputs mean, which to pick for a task.

query.description: What to look up, in plain words and up to 500 characters, e.g. `how to prompt seedance camera moves`

tools.name: generate_models
tools.description: Searches the models generate can run, by what they do (`query`) or by id, with a cursor for the next page.

category.description: Only models in this category, e.g. `text-to-image`, `image-to-video`

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of a previous result, for the page after it; omit for the first page

endpoint_id.description: Endpoint ids to look up directly instead of searching, e.g. `fal-ai/flux/dev`

expand.description: Extra fields to include per model: `openapi-3.0`, `enterprise_status`

limit.description: How many models to return per page, 1 to 100; default 20

status.description: `deprecated` or `all` to include models past their prime; omit for active models

tools.name: generate_pricing
tools.description: A model's price per unit, which generate bills against your credits.

endpoint_id.description: A model's endpoint id, as generate models lists it, e.g. `fal-ai/flux/dev`

tools.name: generate_schema
tools.description: A model's input and output schema: what generate's `input` takes. `openapi` gives the full OpenAPI document.

endpoint_id.description: A model's endpoint id, as generate models lists it, e.g. `fal-ai/flux/dev`

format.description: `compact` (the default) returns the model's catalog entry; `openapi` adds its full OpenAPI 3.0 document, with every input and output field

tools.name: generate_status
tools.description: Follows a generate job: its status (`status`), its output once COMPLETED (`result`, which settles the bill), or `cancel`.

action.description: `status` (the default) reports where the job is; `result` fetches its output once COMPLETED, which settles the bill; `cancel` stops a job that is still queued or running

endpoint_id.description: A model's endpoint id, as generate models lists it, e.g. `fal-ai/flux/dev`

logs.description: Include the job's logs with its status

request_id.description: The job's `request_id`, as generate returned it, with the endpoint_id it ran on

tools.name: generate_upload
tools.description: Opens an upload slot for a model input that takes a file's URL (a reference image, an audio clip to transform). PUT the file's bytes to `uploadUrl` (on this server, valid 15 minutes) with the `headers` given, e.g. `curl -T file.png -H 'Content-Type: image/png' "$uploadUrl"`, then pass `fileUrl` to the model.

contentType.description: The file's MIME type, e.g. `image/png`; PUT the bytes with this Content-Type

fileName.description: The file's name with its extension, e.g. `hero.png`, up to 255 characters

tools.name: generate_animate_3d
tools.description: Rigs a humanoid character GLB, e.g. one generate_3d made, and bakes animation clips onto that one skeleton: a GLB per `animation_action_ids` entry from Meshy's animation library, plus walking and running (Meshy rigging: `meshy/rigging/multi-animation`). The 3d reference of the model-catalog skill lists the clip ids games use. Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

animation_action_ids.description: Up to 10 clips from Meshy's animation library, one GLB each, e.g. 0 for Idle

model_url.description: The character's GLB, e.g. generate 3d's model_glb

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_3d
tools.description: Generates a textured 3D model (GLB) from a prompt, or from an image when `image_url` is given (Meshy 7.1: `meshy/v7.1/text-to-3d`, `meshy/v7.1/image-to-3d`); a low `target_polycount` suits games. To animate a character, model it with `pose_mode` and pass its `model_glb` to generate_animate_3d. Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

image_url.description: An image's URL, e.g. from generate upload

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

pose_mode.description: Model a character in this pose, which rigs cleanly in animate-3d

prompt.description: What to model; needed without image_url

target_polycount.description: The mesh's polygon budget, 100 to 300,000; the model's default is 30,000. Games suit 5,000 to 15,000 for a prop, 15,000 to 40,000 for a hero character

topology.description: The mesh's faces: `triangle` (the model's default) keeps detail, `quad` gives smoother surfaces

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates images from a prompt, or edits and combines reference images when `image_urls` is given (GPT Image 2.5: `openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/text-to-image`, `openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/edit`). `background: transparent` makes sprites and props with no background to remove. Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

background.description: `transparent` leaves no background, for sprites and props; `opaque` always fills one; `auto` lets the model choose. Omit for the model's default

image_size.description: A preset; pass `{width, height}` through options for an exact size

items.description: An image's URL, e.g. from generate upload

num_images.description: How many images to make from the one prompt, 1 to 4; omit for the model's default

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

prompt.description: What to draw, or with image_urls how to edit or combine them, up to 5,000 characters, e.g. `pixel-art knight sprite, side view`

quality.description: Rendering quality from `low` (quick drafts) to `max`; higher takes longer and may cost more (see generate pricing). `auto` lets the model choose; omit for the model's default

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_music
tools.description: Composes music from a prompt: genre, mood, instruments, structure (ElevenLabs Music v2.5: `elevenlabs/music/v2.5`). Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

force_instrumental.description: true makes a track with no vocals; omit to let the prompt decide

music_length_ms.description: The track's length in milliseconds, 3,000 to 600,000 (3 seconds to 10 minutes), e.g. 60000 for a minute; omit for the model's default

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

prompt.description: The music to compose, up to 5,000 characters: genre, mood, instruments, tempo, structure, e.g. `upbeat chiptune boss battle loop, 140 bpm`

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_sound
tools.description: Generates a sound effect from a description: a jump, a hit, an explosion, ambience (ElevenLabs Sound Effects: `elevenlabs/sound-effects/v3`). Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

duration_seconds.description: The sound's length in seconds, 0.5 to 30; omit to let the model fit the length to the sound

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_speech
tools.description: Speaks a line of text: dialogue, narration, an announcer (ElevenLabs v4, which takes audio tags for delivery: `elevenlabs/tts/eleven-v4`). Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

voice.description: A voice name, e.g. Rachel, Aria, Roger

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video clip with sound from a prompt, or animates an image when `image_url` is given (Seedance 2.5: `bytedance/seedance-2.5/us/text-to-video`, `bytedance/seedance-2.5/us/image-to-video`). Video takes minutes: expect a `request_id` to follow with generate_status. Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

aspect_ratio.description: The frame's width to height, e.g. `16:9` landscape, `9:16` portrait, `1:1` square; `auto` lets the model choose, e.g. from image_url. Omit for the model's default

generate_audio.description: false makes a silent clip; omit for the model's default, which generates sound with the video

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

resolution.description: The clip's resolution; higher takes longer and may cost more (see generate pricing). Omit for the model's default

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: generate_remove_background
tools.description: Cuts the subject out of an image onto a transparent background, for sprites and props; `prompt` names what to keep when the cut is ambiguous (Bria Guided Remove Background: `bria/guided-remove-background`). Billed against your credits; waits up to `wait_seconds`, then returns the `request_id` to follow with generate_status.

image_url.description: An image's URL, e.g. from generate upload

options.description: Any other input the model takes, per generate schema of its endpoint; the fields above win

prompt.description: What to keep, e.g. the knight

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the request id

tools.name: skills
tools.description: The vibedgames game-studio skills: without `name`, every skill and what it is for; with one, its full SKILL.md — how to build, art-direct, add multiplayer to, balance and ship a browser game.

name.description: A skill's name from the list

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Returns the authenticated identity, whether the caller used a session cookie, a session token, an API key or an OAuth token. An OAuth token sees `email` only with the `email` scope, and `role` never. Backs `vg whoami`.
